dossier_meta.catalog_title: Informal Conjecture (uniform twin-width strictly stronger than twin-width)
dossier_meta.statement_text: Uniform twin-width is strictly stronger than twin-width, i.e. there are groups with finite twin-width and infinite uniform twin-width.
dossier_meta.context_text: Uniform twin-width requires a uniform bound on the permutation width of the action of every group element, whereas finite twin-width only requires each action to have finite width individually. Having finite uniform twin-width implies finite twin-width, but the converse is not established. The group of finitely supported permutations on $\mathbb{Z}$ is proposed as a candidate counterexample.
